title: Lule Kebab ala Father Vartan Joulfayan
subtitle: Recipe Formulation Sheet
blurb: Armenian ground-beef kebabs bound with breadcrumb and onion liquid, hand-rolled and grilled or oven-roasted.

source.title: Lule Kebab ala Father Vartan Joulfayan
source.author: Father Vartan Joulfayan

summary: Just as there are numerous recipes and spellings for other Armenian foods, lule kebab is no exception. This is Father Vartan Joulfayan's savory version — notable for retaining the onion and garlic liquid released during processing rather than draining it, which is what keeps a lean grind moist on the grill.
scalingPrinciple: Item A.01 (Lean Ground Beef) is locked at 100.0% as the mathematical baseline. Binder, aromatic, and spice percentages read against that 907 g meat mass — the binder ratio in particular must hold, since too little breadcrumb at a higher meat weight will not carry the extra onion liquid.

rows.name: Lean Ground Beef
rows.role: Primary protein substrate; lean grind relies on the onion liquid and egg for moisture.

rows.name: Onion, quartered
rows.role: Processed very fine — the extracted juice is retained and added to the meat, not discarded.

rows.name: Plain Bread Crumb
rows.role: Primary binder; absorbs the retained onion and garlic liquid.

rows.name: Egg, raw
rows.role: Secondary binder; sets during cooking to hold the lule shape.

rows.name: Fresh Parsley, finely chopped
rows.role: Primary herb; substantial quantity, chopped fine.

rows.name: Salt
rows.role: Seasoning; also aids myosin extraction for a cohesive bind.

matrixFootnote: *The source specifies this recipe in volumetric kitchen units and counts apart from the 2 lb meat weight. All other gram values are standard culinary conversions and are marked accordingly.

mise.label: Onion and Garlic Processing (B.01, B.02)
mise.text: Place the quartered onion and 2 cloves of garlic in a food processor. Process until very finely chopped. Do not discard the juice extracted from the onion and garlic — it will be added to the meat mixture and is the primary moisture source in this lean formulation.

execution.name: Combine Meat and Aromatics
execution.text: Place the meat into a large mixing bowl. Add the processed onion and garlic — along with all of their liquid — to the meat.

execution.name: Add Remaining Ingredients
execution.text: Add the breadcrumb, egg, tomato paste, tomato sauce, lemon juice, parsley, and the full spice block to the meat. Mix well by hand until completely uniform.

execution.name: Portion
execution.text: Using a 1/2 cup measure, make 12 balls.

execution.name: Shape and Grill
execution.params: Until cooked through | Outdoor grill or grill pan
execution.text: Roll each ball into the traditional lule (sausage-like) shape and grill until cooked through. An outdoor grill or an indoor grill pan may be used.

execution.name: Oven Alternative
execution.text: If outdoor grilling isn't an option, place the kebabs on a roasting rack over a foil-lined baking pan. Bake at 375°F for about 35 minutes, turning them after about 20 minutes.

directive: Retain every drop of the onion and garlic liquid. At 2 lb of lean grind this liquid, absorbed into the breadcrumb, is the difference between a juicy lule and a dry one — draining the processor bowl is the single most common way this recipe fails.
